source: Observed native AWS controls only; primary documentation is cited separately
cleanup: All exact-owned EIPs, ENIs, root volume, IGW, subnet and VPC verified absent; instance verified terminated. AWS retains terminated-instance descriptions and immutable provider history.

conclusions.finding: AllocateAddress with Domain=vpc and with omitted Domain both return domain vpc, PublicIpv4Pool amazon, NetworkBorderGroup us-east-1 and independent AllocationId/PublicIp values.

DescribeAddresses combines AllocationIds and PublicIps by UNION, not intersection; duplicate allocation IDs deduplicate. Unknown or malformed allocation IDs fail the whole request with InvalidAllocationID.NotFound, including mixed owned+missing selectors.
Association without a VPC-attached IGW fails Gateway.NotAttached. Attaching the IGW admits association to an unattached ENI even without an IGW route. This is not evidence of packet reachability.

Reassociating the same EIP to the same primary target with AllowReassociation=false succeeds and retains its association ID. Moving to another ENI with false fails Resource.AlreadyAssociated without mutation. Omission and explicit true both permit moving.

A free EIP may replace the target's existing EIP even with AllowReassociation=false. The displaced EIP remains allocated and becomes unassociated. The flag protects the source EIP association, not the target's occupancy.

One ENI can hold two EIPs on distinct primary/secondary private addresses. Unassigning the EIP-associated secondary private address SUCCEEDS and implicitly disassociates that EIP while retaining its allocation. The primary-address EIP is unchanged.

Deleting an unattached ENI with an associated primary EIP SUCCEEDS and implicitly disassociates the EIP while retaining the allocation. Deleting an ENI attached to a stopped instance fails InvalidParameterValue ('currently in use').
ReleaseAddress on an associated nondefault-VPC EIP fails InvalidIPAddress.InUse. After disassociation release succeeds. Repeating release by the old AllocationId fails InvalidAllocationID.NotFound.

Repeating DisassociateAddress immediately with the just-successfully-disassociated association ID returns InvalidAssociationID.NotFound. Preserve this observed divergence from the API documentation's unconditional idempotency statement.

The auto-public instance loses its ephemeral IPv4 on stop, gets a different ephemeral IPv4 on start, replaces it with the EIP on association, and gets another ephemeral IPv4 on EIP disassociation. Ephemeral ENI association has IpOwnerId amazon and no AllocationId/AssociationId. Elastic ENI association has the account owner and both IDs.

EIP association and public IPv4 projection persist while stopped. Associating an EIP to a stopped instance succeeds. With two attached ENIs the InstanceId selector fails InvalidInstanceID; explicit ENI succeeds. Detaching a secondary ENI preserves its EIP association but removes InstanceId from the address projection.
Terminating the instance deletes its DeleteOnTermination primary ENI and root volume, and disassociates but does not release the primary EIP.

Authorized DryRun bypasses missing parameters, missing/malformed allocation or association IDs, association conflicts, private-address validation, invalid Describe filter, invalid allocation Domain/PublicIpv4Pool and associated-release state: DryRunOperation. Exceptions observed before DryRun: malformed public IP in DescribeAddresses, malformed AllocateAddress.Address and malformed AllocateAddress.NetworkBorderGroup return InvalidParameterValue.

Actual AssociateAddress validates missing allocation before malformed ENI (InvalidAllocationID.NotFound); malformed/unassigned private address returns InvalidParameterValue even without IGW. Both AllocationId and PublicIp, or deprecated PublicIp alone, return InvalidParameterCombination. The both-target case used an all-zero instance ID, which AWS calls malformed, so it does NOT establish valid-target selector-conflict precedence.

nonobservations: Default-VPC associated release is documentation-only because only fresh owned nondefault VPC resources were authorized.
Quota exhaustion is documentation-only; default is five per Region, not a measurement of this account's quota.
No denied-principal IAM capture, BYOIP, IPAM, CoIP, Wavelength, transfer, address recovery or dual-stack DNS controls.
No native packet-reachability claim; no IGW route was installed.
IGW detach with an EIP on an unattached ENI versus a stopped-instance ENI was requested after capture and was not exercised before teardown.

No-auto-launch EIP disassociation and DescribeNetworkInterfaceAttribute associatePublicIpAddress were requested after capture and were not exercised; the one-instance-total safety bound precluded a replacement guest.
Secondary-private-address reassignment moving its EIP is primary-documentation-only; this capture exercised unassignment and ENI deletion instead.
